# ConfigProvider ## Overview The `ConfigProvider` component provides a React context for configuring global settings across all Bulma UI components. Its `classPrefix` is applied automatically to **all Bulma CSS classes**, including both main component classes (like `button`, `box`, `title`) and helper/modifier classes (like `is-primary`, `has-text-centered`, `m-4`), allowing you to namespace Bulma classes to avoid conflicts with other CSS frameworks or customize the class naming convention. --- ## Import ```tsx import { ConfigProvider, useConfig } from '@allxsmith/bestax-bulma'; ``` --- ## Hooks ### useConfig Returns the current configuration context values. ```tsx const { classPrefix } = useConfig(); ``` ### useClassPrefix Convenience hook that returns just the classPrefix string (or empty string if not set). ```tsx const classPrefix = useClassPrefix(); ``` --- ## Usage Examples ### Basic Usage with Class Prefix Use `ConfigProvider` to add a prefix to all Bulma CSS classes within its scope: ```tsx import { ConfigProvider, Box, Title, Button, Notification, } from '@allxsmith/bestax-bulma'; function App() { return (
Prefixed Bulma Components

This demonstrates using ConfigProvider with{' '} classPrefix="bestax-" to add the "bestax-" prefix to all component CSS classes. This is useful when integrating Bulma with other CSS frameworks or when you need to namespace Bulma classes to avoid conflicts.

Tip: Open your browser's developer tools and inspect the DOM elements below. You'll see that all Bulma CSS classes have the "bestax-" prefix applied. {/* This Box will have classes: - bestax-box (main class) - bestax-mt-4 (helper class) - bestax-p-4 (helper class) */} Prefixed Components {/* This Title will have classes: - bestax-title (main class) - bestax-is-4 (modifier class) */}

All components inside this ConfigProvider will have their CSS classes prefixed with "bestax-". This allows you to use Bulma alongside other CSS frameworks without class name conflicts.

Standard Components (No Prefix)

Components outside the ConfigProvider use standard Bulma classes without any prefix.

); } ``` ### Nested ConfigProviders ConfigProviders can be nested. An inner provider replaces the outer one's settings rather than adding to them, so inside it any setting it leaves out is back to its default: ```tsx function NestedExample() { return ( Outer Prefix (outer-) Inner Prefix (inner-) ); } ``` ### Where Portaled Content Goes `portalContainer` sets where portaled content goes when it has no target of its own. That covers a [`Portal`](https://bestax.io/docs/api/helpers/portal) with no `container`, and what the library's components portal, such as the panel `Popover` renders with `appendToBody`, a `Modal` or `Dialog` with `portal` set to `true`, a `Toast`, or a `Sidebar`. It takes an element or a `document.querySelector` selector. Unset, that content goes to `document.body`. A target a component is given still wins, such as a `Modal`'s `portal` selector or a `Toast`'s `container`. And `portalContainer` only changes where portaled content goes: a component that renders in place, like a `Modal` without `portal` or a `Toast` with `inline`, still does. `document.body` is outside any styles scoped to where the content was declared: a scoped `Theme`'s variables, or a shadow root's stylesheets. To keep them, render an element inside that area and make it the `portalContainer`, held in state from a ref callback. Below, the panel keeps the purple primary its `Theme` sets, which it would lose at the end of the page: ```tsx live function ThemedOverlays() { const [overlays, setOverlays] = useState(null); return ( Open} >
); } ``` A selector can't find an element inside a shadow root, since `document.querySelector` doesn't look there, so in a shadow root pass the element itself, as above. Content that portals before the element is set goes to `document.body` and moves when it is, which remounts it and resets its state, as [`Portal`'s `container`](https://bestax.io/docs/api/helpers/portal#into-a-container) describes. A nested provider like this one needs the class prefix and icon library repeated if your app sets them (see [Nested ConfigProviders](https://bestax.io/docs/api/helpers/config#nested-configproviders)). What gets portaled is `position: fixed`, so put the element where no ancestor has a `transform`, `filter`, `backdrop-filter`, `perspective`, `will-change: transform`, or a `contain` that includes `paint` or `layout`. Any of those becomes the containing block for the overlays and panels, which then cover or line up against that ancestor instead of the viewport. An ancestor that starts a stacking context, with a `z-index` or `isolation: isolate`, keeps them inside it, under anything the page stacks above it. `NotificationContainer` portals its status region along with its notifications, so the `portalContainer` also decides where announcements come from. Keep it out of any `aria-hidden` ancestor, which takes the region out of the accessibility tree and silences them. ### Using Configuration in Custom Components Access the configuration in your own components using the `useConfig` hook: ```tsx import { useConfig } from '@allxsmith/bestax-bulma'; function CustomComponent() { const { classPrefix } = useConfig(); const className = classPrefix ? `${classPrefix}custom-component` : 'custom-component'; return (
My custom component with prefix: {classPrefix || 'none'}
); } ``` --- ## Use Cases ### Framework Integration When integrating Bulma with other CSS frameworks like Bootstrap or Tailwind CSS: ```tsx ``` This ensures all Bulma classes are prefixed with `bestax-`, preventing conflicts with other framework classes. ### Multi-tenant Applications For applications that need to support different styling themes or brands: ```tsx ``` ### Component Library Wrapping When wrapping Bulma UI components in your own component library: ```tsx ``` --- ## Notes - The `classPrefix` is applied to **all Bulma classes**: - Main component classes (e.g., `button` → `bestax-button`, `box` → `bestax-box`) - Helper/modifier classes (e.g., `is-primary` → `bestax-is-primary`, `has-text-centered` → `bestax-has-text-centered`) - Spacing classes (e.g., `m-4` → `bestax-m-4`, `p-2` → `bestax-p-2`) - All other Bulma utility classes - Changes to the `classPrefix` will affect all child components immediately - If no `classPrefix` is provided, components use standard Bulma class names - The ConfigProvider must wrap all components that should inherit the configuration --- ## TypeScript Support Full TypeScript support is included: ```tsx interface ConfigContextProps { classPrefix?: string; iconLibrary?: 'fa' | 'mdi' | 'ion' | 'material-icons' | 'material-symbols'; portalContainer?: string | HTMLElement; } interface ConfigProviderProps { children: ReactNode; classPrefix?: string; iconLibrary?: 'fa' | 'mdi' | 'ion' | 'material-icons' | 'material-symbols'; portalContainer?: string | HTMLElement; } ``` --- ## Props | Prop | Type | Description | | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `children` | `ReactNode` | The child components that will inherit the configuration settings. | | `classPrefix` | `string` | Optional prefix to add to all Bulma CSS classes. Useful for namespacing when integrating with other frameworks. | | `iconLibrary` | `'fa' \| 'mdi' \| 'ion' \| 'material-icons' \| 'material-symbols'` | Default icon library for all child components. | | `portalContainer` | `string` \| `HTMLElement` | Where portaled content goes when it has no target of its own: what a `Portal` without a `container` renders, and what the library's components portal, such as `Popover`'s `appendToBody` panel or a `Modal` with `portal`. An element, or a `document.querySelector` selector. Unset, or a selector that matches nothing, it goes to `document.body`. A target a component is given still wins. |
